title: Cua Spaces
brief: A free full-desktop Space for every agent — macOS VMs on machines you own or in your own cloud (Apple silicon Macs for macOS Spaces, Docker or Podman for Linux), connectable to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Cline, Kiro and OpenClaw through the Cua MCP. Its Teleport feature moves an app's whole session (tabs, profile, sign-ins) from your Mac into a Space, with nothing read until you approve and Touch ID gating on sensitive items.
details: Cua Spaces gives every AI agent a free full desktop — a "Space" running as a VM or container on your Mac, machines you own, or your own cloud, streamed to you as a live desktop via Cua's RCDP remote desktop protocol (low latency over QUIC on local networks). Its Teleport feature moves an entire app session — open tabs, profile, sign-ins — from your Mac into a Space as an encrypted session bundle that nothing reads until you approve, with Touch ID gating on sensitive items and end-to-end sealing to the Space's own key. Spaces come agent-ready with permissions granted and tools installed; Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Cline, Kiro, and OpenClaw connect through the Cua MCP. Spaces on your own machines are free (hosted relay free during early access); the stack is source-available under FSL-1.1-MIT, converting to MIT two years after each release, with Cua Driver and Lume under MIT. Note: anonymous usage telemetry is on by default but can be switched off in settings. From the Cua team (trycua/cua on GitHub).
